description: The Water Distribution Infrastructure Model is a simulation model of an urban water distribution system deposited by Kambiz Rasoulkhani of Texas A&M University at the Dutch DANS data station. The dataset page read on 2026-09-28 describes source code that couples the renewal decisions of the agencies that run the network with its physical components, so that users can simulate how the infrastructure changes under stressors such as population change and fluctuating funding, and measure long-term resilience by spotting regime shifts and tipping points in network performance. The deposit holds a small open zip file of about 14 KB and a restricted PDF titled source code of agent classes, whose name suggests an agent-based design. Coverage is a generic or case-study city; the study area was not stated in the part read. Access is free under the DANS Licence as named, but the code PDF must be requested. Caveats: the programming language, data inputs and case study were not read, and the code is supplied as a PDF, not a repository. It supports water utility resilience and renewal planning studies, such as testing whether a funding cut pushes pipe condition past a tipping point. No related water network renewal model record is catalogued.
